Progress Feedback

3

Coaching Methodology

Progress you can understand.

Progress feedback means Sandy watches what is becoming reliable in live training, identifies the next useful problem, and gives students and families clear feedback along the way. Want to see what that feedback looks like? Preview the Progress Report Card.

One class can show where you are starting. Consistent training gives Sandy enough repeated situations to see what is changing and what needs a different challenge. That is why training is organized as a 12-week first term rather than a collection of unrelated drop-ins.

Why a training term instead of random drop-ins?

Skill studies generally use repeated practice over weeks, not isolated sessions. The 12-week track gives Sandy repeated opportunities to observe the same student across changing partners and problems. The 12-week term is an academy coaching structure, not a claim that research has established 12 weeks as the universally optimal BJJ dose.

After Your First Term

Longer-term options are a later decision.

Core Culture Review looks at what is working, reviews schedule fit, and helps you choose the next arrangement available under current policy. Paths may include renewed Core Culture, Annual Track, Elite Concierge, flexible access, a pause, or the end of training.

Adult Private Coaching Intensive $7,150 / 12 weeks

Continuation-only adult offer with six scheduled 60-minute private sessions alongside current adult group-training limits. Application and schedule review are required; the Adult Core Culture guarantee does not automatically apply.

Review Intensive →
Annual Track Youth $2,100 · Adult $2,650 · Community $2,250 / four 12-week cycles

For students continuing after an initial 12-week term. Annual Track covers four 12-week cycles, with three planned classes per week and a schedule and progress review after each cycle. It does not add another uniform and does not include the 30-Day Training Fit Guarantee.
